questions.prompt: What APIs does AzureHound use to enumerate an Entra ID/Azure environment?
options: It exploits a vulnerability in the Entra ID login page
The same Microsoft Graph API and Azure REST API that legitimate administration and reporting tools use every day
It requires physical access to a domain controller
It only works against on-premises Active Directory, not cloud
questions.explanation: AzureHound is built entirely on legitimate Graph and Azure REST API calls — nothing about it requires exploiting anything, which is exactly what makes it hard to distinguish from routine administration.

questions.prompt: What is described as one of the highest-confidence single detection indicators for unmodified AzureHound usage?
options: The specific time of day it runs
Its distinctive default User-Agent string, "azurehound/<version>", unless an operator deliberately changes it
The number of licenses assigned to the tenant
questions.explanation: The default azurehound/<version> User-Agent string is a high-confidence indicator specifically because most operators don't bother changing it.

questions.prompt: Why doesn't AzureHound need to run from inside the victim's network?
options: Both Microsoft Graph and Azure REST APIs are reachable externally with a valid token
It requires installation on a domain-joined device
It only works through a VPN connection to the tenant
questions.explanation: Since Graph and Azure REST APIs are externally reachable given a valid token, a stolen or forged token used from anywhere outside the victim's network still produces the same enumeration signature.

questions.prompt: What real-world attribution does this lesson cite for AzureHound/BloodHound-suite misuse?
options: It has only ever been used in authorized penetration tests
Microsoft has publicly attributed usage to the Russia-affiliated actor tracked as Void Blizzard
It has never been observed in a real intrusion
It's exclusively used by financially motivated ransomware groups
questions.explanation: Microsoft's own threat intelligence has documented this tooling's use by Void Blizzard — confirming this is a real, observed nation-state technique, not a hypothetical red-team-only concern.
